title: Bempikibart in Alopecia Areata: A 33-Patient Signal Is Not Yet a Win Over JAK Inhibitors
summary: Q32 Bio nearly doubled after a 33-patient, single-arm Phase 2a readout. The investable questions are whether efficacy survives randomization, whether responses persist after treatment stops, and whether a larger safety database can support a differentiated place beside JAK inhibitors.
source_status: Complete professional English adaptation of the approved public Drugnews Facebook/Dcard longform; argument order, clinical figures, investment interpretation, caveats and references retained
cover_image_alt: A 33-patient SIGNAL-AA Part B Phase 2a signal and the evidence required before the program can be considered de-risked
homepage_cover_image_alt: Bempikibart has earned a larger test in alopecia areata, but has not yet beaten JAK inhibitors
core_judgments: The 33-patient, single-arm Phase 2a readout is sufficient to advance bempikibart, but the absence of placebo control or a JAK head-to-head comparison means it has not demonstrated superiority over JAK inhibitors.
The same 10 responders produce 40.0% in the 25-patient mITT set and 30.3% in the 33-patient ITT set, illustrating why denominator, missing-data rules and analysis populations matter in small trials.

The next valuation inflection points are Week 52 durability, efficacy replication under randomized control, safety at larger exposure and whether the planned registration-directed program actually starts in the first half of 2027.
